label: Bible Study
prompt: But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep _____ before him.
verse: But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.
note: After a string of woes against idols, the true God appears — and everyone hushes.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by _____.
verse: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.
note: John closes by asking that the friends be greeted by name — not 'everybody,' but everybody personally.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp _____ sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.
verse: And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth went a sharp twoedged sword: and his countenance was as the sun shineth in his strength.
note: In John's vision a sharp twoedged sword comes from Jesus' mouth — Hebrews 4:12 says the same of God's word.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a _____ mind: for the LORD searcheth all hearts, and understandeth all the imaginations of the thoughts: if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever.
verse: And thou, Solomon my son, know thou the God of thy father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for the LORD searcheth all hearts, and understandeth all the imaginations of the thoughts: if thou seek him, he will be found of thee; but if thou forsake him, he will cast thee off for ever.
note: David's charge to Solomon: serve God wholeheartedly, because he searches every heart and motive.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Brethren, I count not myself to have _____: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
verse: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
note: Paul admits he hasn't 'apprehended' — laid hold of — the prize yet. So: forget what's behind and reach forward.
